triggers.why: A README for a CLI, including install and first run: the core qualified case.
A how-to must follow a renamed flag; command accuracy against the product is the method's subject.
A runbook with symptoms, verification and rollback is a documented type with its own checklist.
An ADR is a documentation genre with status rules the method owns.
A documentation translation that must stay in step with its original.
Release notes written from the actual diff, with compatibility as the leading concern.
Reviewing an API reference against the implementation is documentation review, not code work.
A code refactor. Implementation work belongs to a code method, not to documentation.
AGENTS.md changes agent behaviour; it is not edited by an ordinary documentation workflow.
Running a test suite and reporting failures involves no document.
An ordinary letter to a colleague: not product documentation.
Marketing landing copy is a promotional genre, outside this method's scope.
A commit message belongs to the change workflow, not to the documentation set.
